title: Scheme manifest and dispatch table
description: What makes one rail, and what happens to every message in its catalogue. See design/05 and design/11.

messages.description: The message catalogue. Every message has exactly one disposition.

repliesTo.description: The messages of this scheme this one answers, each sent out (Issue I-235, R-09-211): a reply's wait is measured from the message it answers.

file.description: The rules of this message's file, which the File API reads from the active distribution (Issue I-159, R-09-209). A value not declared is the installation's setting.

namePattern.description: A regular expression the file's name (without an encryption extension) matches in full.

extensions.description: The extensions the file's name may end in, each with its dot; an encrypted file may add .gpg, .pgp or .asc.

maxBytes.description: The largest file taken, in bytes.

uniqueName.description: Whether a file of this message may come only once under a name.

encrypted.description: true: the file MUST arrive encrypted; false: it MUST NOT. Not declared: either.

start.description: Starts a platform workflow with this leg in its slot. The dispatch table says what payment the message starts: kind, direction and, where the platform workflow depends on it, segment. Workflow-select reads them to choose the platform workflow (R-05-42).

refuseLeg.description: Inward only: the leg that fills the platform workflow's scheme-refuse slot.

direction.description: The direction of the payment the message starts, not of the message: an employer's salary file comes in and starts an outward payment.

segment.description: The segment of the payment, where the platform workflow depends on it: an outward payment's. A code of the segment registry (Part 2).

deliver.description: Delivered to a running workflow that awaits it.

families.description: The families the front door tells apart, read from the message (for a WPS acknowledgement, the acknowledged file's family from its name). An await may name one (R-05-44).

correlationMap.description: A map activity (direction in) that reads the keys of the payment the file answers from the file: its name and content (Issue I-267, I-160 (2), R-09-212). Without one the front door matches the keys the sender gives and, failing those, the stem of the file name.

reconcile.description: A scheme's report, reconciled on arrival, not routed (Issue I-164, R-09-210): the map reads the scheme's layout into report lines, the activity reconciles them, and the period says which payments the report covers, so a payment it does not name is a break.

period.description: The time the report covers, ending at its arrival: an ISO 8601 duration of days, hours or minutes.

resolutions.description: The messages of this scheme that start an order to resolve a break of this report (R-09-250, Issue I-168): exception-request names an inward message that starts a request (kind request, on p.wf.request.v1), return one that starts a return (kind return). Each is started from the break's order document (th-break-order/1) once a bank approver consents. A scheme that names none is not offered them (lint L62).

sentBy.description: Outbound message: the exchange block that sends it.

planned.description: Not yet defined. Blocks publication of the pack.
